Subsea motor component without a propeller or nozzle; requires a speed controller and integration into a vehicle or tool.
Scanning imaging sonar accessory for underwater navigation, not a complete ROV.
Underwater propulsion component for integration into ROVs, AUVs or surface vessels, not a complete robot.
Autonomy software and cloud infrastructure for integration into partner machines, not a complete robot model.

Fully managed shelf-intelligence service using robot-powered scanning. The offering is not a separately specified robot chassis; a related scanner is not identified as an independent catalog model by this review.
Platform-agnostic autonomy software and development tools; the aircraft it controls are separately named systems, not additional Hivemind robot models.
Autonomous-driving integration stack combining software, compute and sensors. This is not a complete vehicle; classifying the stack does not validate the separate Robotaxi listing.

Plant-level vision, decision and actuation technology integrated into agricultural machinery. The generic technology name does not identify a complete autonomous vehicle or a particular John Deere sprayer configuration.
Single-pixel light sensor module for a Cubelets construction; needs integration with other blocks and power to perform a robot application.
Infrared proximity-sensing Cubelets module, not a complete robot construction.
Programmable multicolor LED output Cubelet; a module for a larger construction rather than a complete robot kit.
Raspberry Pi interface/controller system for LEGO motors and sensors. Kits require separately supplied LEGO parts; generic controller kits are not counted as assembled robot models.

Handheld ground-control station with display, joysticks, telemetry and battery; controls a separately supplied aircraft. Its runtime and mass are not aircraft specifications. A zero-dollar shop placeholder is not a free robot offer.

Staffed Robotic Security Operations Center provides remote monitoring, piloting and mission oversight. It is a managed operations service, not a robot chassis; Guardian and DroneDog are separately named systems.

Fixed-camera sensing system mounted on shelves, bins, walls or ceilings, with wall or battery power. It supplements the mobile Tally robot with frequent targeted scans; the battery option does not imply a mobile robot chassis.

AI Robot Cloud is shared cloud-based robot intelligence and service infrastructure. ARC Eye supplies localization and ARC Brain plans movement/tasks for connected robots. It is not a physical robot model; historical deployment language is not a current availability or launch claim.

Cordless electric broom guided by its operator: manufacturer instructions say to pull the handle back and glide it over the floor. Powered brushing and a rechargeable battery do not make it an autonomous vacuum robot. The original source model remains in the inventory without claiming catalog robot coverage.

Smart upright scrubber dryer operated by a person using a one-piece handle with one or two hands and foot-pedal activation. Digital reports, intelligent sensors and an app do not establish autonomous navigation. It remains distinct from autonomous CC1 and MT1 robots; no manual appliance is imported as a robot.

Fixed pedestal-mounted gate-access and camera unit. Visitor checks, credentials, AI analysis and battery backup do not imply a self-propelled robot. Commercial and Residential editions share AVA Gen4 hardware; neither is imported as a mobile robot.

Wall- or pole-mounted security camera, display and talk-down unit with mains power and backup battery. Detection and deterrence are automated but the unit does not patrol autonomously. This nonrobot sensing hardware is kept separate from ROAMEO.

Solar/battery security observation tower or trailer carrying ROSA sensors on a telescoping mast. Manufacturer placement instructions require flatbed delivery and forklift placement. Mobile means relocatable equipment, not autonomous self-propelled patrol; Mini, 180 and 360 packages are not counted as robots.

Manufacturer announcement identifies RADCam as a residential security camera with AI interaction and alerts. It has no autonomous patrol chassis. The old /radcam URL now redirects to ROSA; that redirect is not treated as proof that RADCam and ROSA are the same hardware.

Agentic AI incident-response software verifies events, invokes talk-down, calls contacts and records outcomes. It can run with RAD equipment and compatible third-party cameras. Agent, Edge and supporting modules are software editions, not separate physical robot models.

Manufacturer brochure identifies K1 Laser as a LiDAR sensor for security/crowd analytics, with flexible mounting and scalable sensor deployment. It is a fixed sensor product, not an additional mobile patrol robot. Generic redirected product HTML is not evidence of the historical item, and detection accuracy/privacy/weather guarantees are not imported.

Manufacturer identifies an integrated AS/RS with HaiClimber robot units, workstations, racking and HaiQ orchestration. Double-deep storage and modular vertical/horizontal travel describe the configured system. System throughput/density are installation-dependent, not specifications of one robot. Named HaiClimber unit is separately documented in the catalog.

Manufacturer explicitly describes a modular ASRS combining automated case-handling robots, workstations, racking, containers and HaiQ software for goods-to-person workflows. Different robot configurations can be used; no single System 1 hardware model or universal picking/cost guarantee is invented.

Integrated warehouse system combines case-handling robots with heavy-duty companion AMRs, workstations, racking and HaiQ software. Mixed bulk/pallet and individual tote handling are system capabilities, not one robot model. Manufacturer improvement factors are not guaranteed results for every installation.

Integrated warehouse system combines case-handling robots and fast-transit companion AMRs, workstations and orchestration. Triple-deep storage and mixed-container workflows belong to the configured system. Linked A42T-E2 and K50 physical robots are separately documented; model-page 30 kg tote rating is not replaced with broader system-page 50 kg marketing.

evidence.publisher: Iris Automation — April 20, 2022 manufacturer announcement distributed by PRNewswire

decisions.note: Ground-based optical airspace surveillance/detect-and-avoid equipment with networkable nodes, not an aircraft or complete robot. Manufacturer release identifies 360-degree ground-based monitoring and traffic-data sharing. No blanket BVLOS permission, collision-prevention guarantee or independent regulatory certification inferred.

evidence.publisher: uAvionix / Airwise Solutions — August 18, 2026 joint announcement published by Airwise Solutions

decisions.note: Joint provider announcement identifies uAvionix FlightLine as an ADS-B surveillance data service powered by the FlightStation receiver network and supplied through an API. It is not an Iris-manufactured airframe or separate robot model. Data covers cooperative aircraft; no universal aircraft visibility, BVLOS authorization, FAA endorsement or safety guarantee inferred.

Manufacturer identifies AstroRinse as the separate filter-cleaning/charging station in the AquaSense X ecosystem. Station uses a rotating water nozzle and debris collection bin after the robot is docked. It is accessory equipment, not an independently mobile pool robot. No universal automatic return, maintenance-free interval or exact regional bundle inferred.

Manufacturer ASTRO portfolio names RST-135, RST-135E, RST-300 and RST-2000F as telescope pointing/tracking mounts for observation, including remote GOTO and autoguiding. These are actuated instrument-mount components, not standalone mobile/humanoid robot models. Generic series does not identify an exact mount or establish common precision, load or safety ratings across variants.

Manufacturer brochure explicitly includes six mBot2 coding robots, charging equipment, storage, activity map and teaching materials for classroom use. This is a multi-robot education bundle, not a seventh model. No new robot SKU or automatic exact bundle generation is claimed.

Manufacturer history uses clean robot for multiple NS, NX and NT semiconductor wafer/LCD-handling series, rather than a uniquely named model. Source title is generic. Its floor-cleaning/navigation marketing fields are not validated by that literature and are not imported. No specific cleanroom arm, floor cleaner or common capability is assumed; this review records generic identity without catalog coverage.

Manufacturer calls Saymo our robot and identifies it as John Mulaney’s sidekick on Everybody’s Live. This is a named robot/television character, not evidence of a separately offered hardware model. Identity is retained without inventing another SKU, assigning it to Gen3 or transferring Gen3 specifications. Robot existence is acknowledged; catalog model coverage is not claimed.
